title: District overlay patch
description: Hand-authored overlay applied after generate_district(seed). Blit only — does not fork the generator. Ticket 07.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. Permanent once shipped.

seed.description: District seed this overlay is authored against. apply_patch still blits regardless; the seed documents intent.

anchors.description: Rect-relative points SimTemplates.stamp converts to absolute and writes onto the map object, so the colony's gates, start tile and well stop being compile-time constants. Same shape as building.schema.json's anchors, and relative for the same reason: this entry is a template that happens to still be stamped at a fixed origin.

tiles.description: Row-major tile enums matching SimTileMap.Tile, length w*h.

tile.description: Rect-relative, like the anchors above and for the same reason: this entry is a template that happens to still be stamped at a fixed origin, and a template may not name an absolute district tile. SimTemplates.stamp adds the rect's origin and appends the result to map.sites, which is what SimBoot.place_loot reads. Same shape and same meaning as building.schema.json's loot.

table.description: The location loot table this site rolls, matching a content/loot entry's `location`. docs/12's five scavenging locations; Milestone 2 authors four of them. Kept in step with loot.schema.json and district.schema.json by hand -- LOCATIONS in check_loot.gd is what asserts nothing names a table nobody wrote.

container.description: When present, this site is not scattered at boot -- SimBoot.place_loot stands a searchable container here holding the same table, and it yields when somebody opens it. The value is what the thing is called out loud ("cupboard", "car boot"); it is prose read only by SimContainers.hud_clause, so it is free text rather than an enum. Searched once and never again: docs/12 puts resource respawn timers on the cut list.

loot.description: Loot sites this template carries with it, template-relative and converted to absolute district tiles on stamp. The district's own sites come from its lootProfile (SimWorldgen's worldgen.sites pass); these are the ones an authored interior owns -- the annex's kitchen scatter and the cupboard in its store room -- and they travel with the template wherever the generator puts it.

roof.description: Roof material. The name resolves through content/dressing/street.json's `roofs` table to the sprite keys the renderer blits -- presentation/roof_look.gd decides cap vs face per tile and which interior tiles take a roof. A material with no table entry draws the procedural wall, which is the supported fallback.

wall.description: Wall material. The name resolves through content/dressing/street.json's `walls` table to the sprite keys the renderer blits -- presentation/roof_look.gd decides cap vs face per tile and which interior tiles take a roof. A material with no table entry draws the procedural wall, which is the supported fallback.

look.description: How this template looks: `{roof, wall}` material names that content/dressing/street.json's `roofs`/`walls` tables resolve to sprite keys. Optional here -- the shipped annex declares it, but the oracle's own fixtures may not. The Godot validator is shallow -- it accepts any object satisfying the top-level required/type check here and never re-checks the enum below at load -- so check_roof_look.gd's LOOK lane is what actually enforces `roof`/`wall` against the enum on every shipped template.
